To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

G72/G30 mice exhibit a reduced activity of complex I, which is accompanied by an impaired capability to maintain synaptic activity and an impaired capability of spatial memory that can be rescued by treatment with NAC.

the humanized transgenic mice expressing the gene locus G72 exhibit a reduced activity of the mitochondrial respiratory chain complex I and a concomitant increase of mitochondrial reactive oxygen species.
(1) G72Tg transgenic mice show mitochondrial dysfunction, synaptic deficits and cognitive impairment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the function of the G72 gene, which is associated with schizophrenia and bipolar disorder, and its impact on brain function and behavior.
the role of the G72/G30 gene locus in psychiatric disorders.
the identification and characterization of the function of novel, anthropoid-primate-specific genes in the pathomechanism and treatment of psychiatric diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the G72 gene is a risk gene for psychiatric disorders and the G72 protein is involved in the pathomechanism.
the G72/G30 locus is not a risk factor for psychiatric diseases.

G72Tgs exhibit a reduced activity of complex I, which leads to an increase in the production of reactive oxygen, and that this in turn leads to an impairment of short-term plasticity in the CA3 region of the hippocampus, which is accompanied by an impairment in spatial learning and memory, and that these deficits can be rescued with N-acetylcysteine treatment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we identified the G72 protein as a novel mitochondrial protein, that G72Tgs are a valid model to study the pathomechanisms underlying psychiatric diseases and that G72-mediated deficits in synaptic plasticity and memory can be rescued by N-acetyl cystein treatment.
the G72Tg mouse model of schizophrenia exhibits cognitive deficits that can be rescued by N-acetyl cystein treatment.
G72Tgs are an animal model for schizophrenia.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the humanized bacterial artificial chromosome transgene mouse expressing human G72 transcripts throughout the brain exhibits mitochondrial dysfunction and cognitive deficits.
G72Tgs have reduced mitochondrial function and that this leads to a cognitive deficit that can be rescued by N-acetyl cystine.
the mitochondrial dysfunction is the cause of cognitive deficits in the G72/G30 transgenic mice.
